header.name: Human AI Interaction (HAI)
header.description: This course teaches students how to design AI systems that prioritize human-centered approaches. It covers topics like how humans think and use computers, the social construct and its impact on technology use, usability, ethics, and trust. Students learn how to transform human needs and limitations into design goals, build interfaces that facilitate easy communication and control, and consider issues such as bias and inequality. The course also highlights methods for evaluating AI systems that focus on people, including interviews, user studies, fairness and transparency tests, and long-term field research. These go beyond technical results to measure real-world usefulness, safety, and user satisfaction.\n\nThis is an advanced course that involves reading research papers from top conferences, writing reviews, and actively participating in class discussions for critical analysis. Students will work on individual projects where they evaluate, design, and build AI systems in different domains. They will give presentations to discuss and critique human-centered design and evaluation approaches for AI systems.
prerequisites_mandatory: Machine Learning (ECE363/ECE563/CSE343/543) or Deep Learning (CSE641) or Artificial Intelligence (CSE 643)

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students would be able to explain human cognitive, social, and ethical factors that shape human–AI interaction and relate them to concrete design requirements for interactive AI systems.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students would be able to apply human-centered design methods and prototyping techniques to create interaction artifacts that improve usability, transparency, and user control in AI-driven applications.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to study AI behavior and user interactions using human-focused evaluation methods, and interpret both qualitative and quantitative data to uncover issues with usability, bias, and safety.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students would be able to design and justify interventions or system changes that improve fairness, trust, and real-world effectiveness, using empirical evidence and ethical reasoning.

lecture_topics: Prompting as an Interface & Human-AI Interaction Design

resources.title: Shneiderman, Ben, Human-Centered AI (Oxford, 2022; online edn, Oxford Academic, 17 Feb. 2022), https://doi.org/10.1093/oso/9780192845290.001.0001, accessed 8 Nov. 2025.
